evals.name: inbox-cleanup
evals.prompt: I have ten unlinked notes in my Tolaria Inbox. Help me decide what to delete, what to connect, and what should become evergreen notes.
evals.expected_output: A capture-to-organize workflow that treats Inbox as derived from unlinked notes and connects surviving notes to useful containers.
assertions: Explains that the Inbox is a derived state, not a folder
Uses the question 'what is this useful for?' or equivalent
Allows deleting weak captures
Connects surviving notes to Projects, Responsibilities, Procedures, Topics, Events, or People
Reserves evergreen notes for reusable timeless ideas

evals.name: project-note-shape
evals.prompt: Create a Tolaria project note for launching a newsletter sponsorship product.
evals.expected_output: A Markdown project note shape with frontmatter and relation conventions that remains portable plain text.
assertions: Classifies the item as a Project
Includes useful frontmatter such as type, status, Workspace, and dates
Uses canonical typed relation fields such as belongs_to, related_to, or has rather than only prose links
Keeps the output readable as plain Markdown

evals.name: implementation-boundary
evals.prompt: Change the Tolaria app so status frontmatter renders as a colored chip.
evals.expected_output: The agent should recognize this as implementation work rather than vault-content organization.
assertions: Recognizes this as app implementation work outside the vault-content scope
Avoids editing vault notes as the main answer
Mentions semantic property rendering or app code behavior

evals.name: system-property-schema
evals.prompt: Create a Tolaria Type note for Projects with sidebar order, sidebar label, color, icon, and pinned status property.
evals.expected_output: A Type note that stores UI preferences as underscore-prefixed system properties while keeping normal semantic fields user-visible.
assertions: Uses underscore-prefixed fields such as _order, _sidebar_label, _color, _icon, and _pinned_properties
Does not use non-underscore fields for internal UI preferences
Uses canonical semantic fields such as type and status where appropriate
Keeps the configuration in Markdown frontmatter rather than app-local state
Mentions that _* fields must be hidden from normal Properties/search/filter surfaces while preserved on disk

evals.name: legacy-title-and-display-name
evals.prompt: Create a new Tolaria Person note for Luca Rossi. Should I include title: in the frontmatter?
evals.expected_output: A Person note that uses an H1 as the display title and avoids writing title: for a new note unless needed as a legacy fallback.
assertions: Uses an H1 heading as the primary display title
Does not add title: automatically for a new note
Uses type: Person or the established vault type convention
Keeps the note readable as plain Markdown

evals.name: legacy-relation-migration
evals.prompt: Some old Tolaria notes use 'Belongs to' and 'Related to' in frontmatter. Normalize them while keeping diffs small.
evals.expected_output: A migration plan that maps humanized relation fields to canonical belongs_to and related_to fields without destructive rewrites.
assertions: Maps Belongs to to belongs_to
Maps Related to to related_to
Preserves unknown frontmatter fields
Warns to inspect nearby notes and report changed files
Keeps rewrites minimal for readable Git diffs

evals.name: frontmatter-parser-boundary
evals.prompt: I am changing Tolaria frontmatter parsing. What schema rules must I preserve around _fields and user-visible properties?
evals.expected_output: A schema-behavior checklist covering _* filtering from UI/search/filter surfaces, preservation on disk, and canonical relation humanization.
assertions: States that _* fields are hidden from Properties, search facets, filters, and normal UI
States that _* fields remain editable in raw editor and preserved on disk
Mentions vault/mod.rs or utils/frontmatter.ts as parser locations
Mentions humanizing belongs_to, related_to, and has in UI
Preserves unknown non-system frontmatter fields
